value.title: rs seat observability — one spine writer, stamped descriptor events, role on the row, reap/close
value.summary: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-07 by plan 139 rs-governance-port (its units u1/u2/u5). Four rs gaps that all bite UI consumers (chainglass, plan 093 reader), measured live 2026-09-06: (1) the spine has three writers so seat.put/tombstone/report.* never fan out on /v1/events and a live cursor burns past them; (2) registry rows carry at=0 and seat.put an empty payload; (3) nothing can set a seat's role, so every card reads ROLE UNKNOWN; (4) no close verb and no reaper, ~716 idle corpses. Make the bus the only spine writer with stamped descriptor payloads; add a role writer/setter/join; add close + reap.

sections.name: goals
value: Every spine row is published through EventBus (store append then broadcast): seat.put, seat.tombstone, report.now, report.state reach a live /v1/events subscriber; no live cursor can advance past an unemitted row.
Descriptor events carry a real `at` and the descriptor as payload (seat.put) / reason (seat.tombstone).
A seat's role is settable (register/adopt --role; a role verb for existing seats), persisted (seat_roles), and joined onto /v1/seats.role and StateCard.role.

A supported teardown: `pij-rs close <id>` tombstones a seat the caller owns; a reaper tombstones rows whose proc{pid,proc_start} is provably dead and whose pane is gone, with a spine event naming the evidence.

sections.name: non_goals
value: No change to delivery semantics (136/137 hold rules) or to the /v1/events frame shape beyond additive fields; payload stays a JSON string.
No migration of the 1456 historical seat.put rows; consumers replay from now.
No role INFERENCE from names or window titles — role is asserted by the owner, not derived.

value.text: Two live /v1/events subscribers (one with `since`, one live-only) both receive a `report now` frame and an `adopt` seat.put frame written while open; measured with chainglass's 4-command control (findings/live-push-recheck-2026-09-06.md). Grep: no `INSERT INTO spine_events` outside crates/store/src/spine.rs.

A fresh adopt's seat.put row has `at` within 1 s of wall clock and a payload that decodes to the SeatDescriptor; seat.tombstone has `at` and reason. Live sqlite proof on the production store after deploy.

`pij-rs adopt %N --harness claude --role prime` then `/v1/seats` shows role=prime; `pij-rs role <id> reviewer` (or the chosen verb) updates it; StateCard.role follows; chainglass renders it without a banner. Ownership: only the seat itself or its parent may set it.

`pij-rs close <id>` on an owned seat writes seat.tombstone with at+reason and the row leaves /v1/seats; the reaper run on the production store tombstones corpses whose pid is dead or whose proc_start no longer matches, and refuses a recycled-pid live process (plan 095 evidence). Count before/after cited.

value.title: Spine: one writer, stamped descriptor events
value.brief: Route ReportService and Registry::put/tombstone through EventBus::publish (or make the bus the Spine impl every writer receives); stamp at; carry the descriptor payload. RED: chainglass's positive control fails on main.

value.title: Role: writer, setter verb, row join
value.brief: `--role` on register/adopt, a setter verb, seat_roles persisted and joined onto /v1/seats + StateCard; ownership check (self or parent).

value.title: Lifecycle: close verb + reaper
value.brief: `pij-rs close <id>` (owner-only tombstone) and a reaper over proc{pid,proc_start}+pane; never trusts pid alone (recycled-identifiers).
